title: Why did the traffic fall every hour after 8 a.m.?
description: The bars after eight in the morning are read one by one and each is taken away from the one before to see how fast the traffic falls. A reason for the fall is found by thinking about where people are by then.
teaching_notes: One idea: subtract neighbouring bars to see a trend, then give a reason for it from daily life. Watch for answers that only say the bars get shorter.

video_script.why: The child subtracts one bar from the next to measure the fall, and gives a reason for it.
video_script.substitution: Take each bar away from the one before it to see the fall, and give a reason from daily life.
video_script.anchor: the horizontal bar graph of vehicles passing a busy crossing in Delhi in each hour from six in the morning to noon
video_script.payoff_line: The traffic fell because most people had already reached work or school

final_answer.value: Open-ended: most people had already reached work or school
final_answer.spoken: most people had already reached work or school, so fewer vehicles were on the road

maths_rules: bars after 8 a.m.: 8-9 1000, 9-10 about 800, 10-11 about 700, 11-12 about 600
video_script.design: One idea: subtract neighbouring bars to measure a fall, then give a reason from daily life. The graph stays on the board all video. The reason is open-ended, so the video gives the worklist's example reason and says so.
open_questions: The question is open-ended. The video gives the worklist's example reason. The 10 to 11 bar of about 700 is read from the worklist, not from the book text.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: take each bar away from the one before. 1000 - 800 = 200; 800 - 700 = 100; 700 - 600 = 100

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, take each bar away from the one before it, to see how fast the traffic falls. One thousand take away eight hundred is two hundred.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Eight hundred take away seven hundred is one hundred.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Seven hundred take away six hundred is also one hundred.

<bookmark mark='smaller'/>The traffic falls every hour, but by a smaller amount each time.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: think about the time of day: after 8 in the morning, fewer people are still travelling; the road gets emptier hour by hour

narration: <bookmark mark='clock'/>Step three, think about the time of day, because traffic follows people. After eight, fewer people are still on the way.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the falls. 200 + 100 + 100 = 400 and 1000 - 600 = 400; the two agree
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, check the falls. Two hundred, one hundred and one hundred make four hundred.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>One thousand take away six hundred is also four hundred, so the two agree.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the traffic fell because most people had already reached work or school
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The traffic fell because most people had already reached work or school.
